resource.name: aws_key_pair
resource.description: Provides an EC2 key pair resource. A key pair is used to control login access to EC2 instances. Currently this resource requires an existing user-supplied key pair. This key pair's public key will be registered with AWS to allow logging-in to EC2 instances. When importing an existing key pair the public key material may be in any format supported by AWS. Supported formats (per the AWS documentation) are: - OpenSSH public key format (the format in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys) - Base64 encoded DER format - SSH public key file format as specified in RFC4716
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_key_pair` Terraform resource manages the registration of an existing SSH key pair's public key with AWS, enabling secure login access to EC2 instances. It is commonly used for configuring SSH-based authentication to virtual machines, facilitating remote management and deployment workflows. Users can import public keys in formats like OpenSSH, Base64-encoded DER, or RFC4716, ensuring compatibility with various key management systems and secure access practices.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_key_pair` resource to create an SSH key pair in AWS by specifying a `key_name` and providing a `public_key`. Users can learn how to securely manage access to EC2 instances by associating a custom public key with the key pair.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_key_pair` resource represents the unique identifier of the key pair, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While not required, this argument can be used to reference or track the key pair within Terraform configurations, enabling users to manage or query the resource in other parts of their infrastructure.

arguments.name: key_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name for the key pair. If neither `key_name` nor `key_name_prefix` is provided, Terraform will create a unique key name using the prefix `terraform-`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `key_name` argument allows users to specify a custom name for the key pair in AWS, enabling easier identification and management of SSH key pairs. If not provided, Terraform generates a unique name with a `terraform-` prefix, making this argument useful for aligning key pair naming with organizational or project-specific conventions.

arguments.name: key_name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `key_name`. If neither `key_name` nor `key_name_prefix` is provided, Terraform will create a unique key name using the prefix `terraform-`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `key_name_prefix` argument in the `aws_key_pair` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for the automatically generated name of the key pair, ensuring uniqueness while avoiding naming conflicts. This is particularly useful for dynamically creating key pairs in environments where explicit naming (`key_name`) is not required, supporting workflows like automated provisioning or ephemeral infrastructure setups.

arguments.name: public_key
arguments.llm_summary: The `public_key` argument in the `aws_key_pair` resource allows users to specify the public key material for an SSH key pair, enabling secure access to EC2 instances. By providing this required string, users define the cryptographic key used for authentication, ensuring controlled and encrypted remote access to cloud resources.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Key-value map of resource tags. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_key_pair` resource allows users to define a key-value map of metadata to categorize and manage the key pair, such as environment identifiers (e.g., "dev" or "prod") or ownership details. Configuring this argument helps streamline resource organization, enables cost tracking, and integrates with provider-level `default_tags` for consistent tagging across AWS resources.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_key_pair` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically propagated to the resource, including inherited tags from the provider's default configuration. This enables consistent tagging for resource organization, cost allocation, and management across AWS environments.

attributes.name: fingerprint
attributes.description: The MD5 public key fingerprint as specified in section 4 of RFC 4716.
